auth: Two tiers. The direct read procedures (assess, identify, explain, variants, walk, origins, history, ...) serve KEYLESS: no key, rate-limited (~100/window), real production-shaped answers. note: The whisper.security graph is two-tier. Tools with _requiresKey:false (== _access "keyless", the direct read procedures: assess, identify, explain, variants, walk, origins, history, ...) run WITHOUT a key, rate-limited (~100/window) with real answers; send X-API-Key to lift the limit. Tools with _requiresKey:true (raw Cypher, the multi-step flows, and submit) need X-API-Key. Each tool carries _docPath/_docsUrl (docsBase + docPath) for its documentation page; flow tools carry _flowRun (POST the slug to the run endpoint, SSE stream).

tools.name: whisper_identify
tools.description: Name the vendor and operator role behind a host or IP in one call. Resolves a host/IP to its canonical vendor, category and operator roles (DNS_OPERATOR / CDN / ORIGIN_AS / MAIL_RECEIVER) with a confidence band.

_exec.cypher: CALL whisper.identify([$v]) YIELD host, vendor_id, canonical_name, category, roles, host_class, band

tools.name: whisper_assess
tools.description: Get a labelled threat posture for a host or IP - malicious, benign, or unknown. Returns a posture label + severity band + sub-labels + coverage + evidence for an indicator; benign-allowlisted vs malicious-evidenced, never a bare score.

_exec.cypher: CALL whisper.assess([$v]) YIELD host, label, band, sub_labels, coverage, evidence

tools.name: whisper_walk
tools.description: Walk the graph to the nearest known vendors behind a host, with the channel and confidence. Structural attribution: returns nearest_known_vendors with the channel (DELEGATED_TO / ORIGIN_AS) and confidence, plus siblings and coverage - explains WHY a host maps to a vendor.

_exec.cypher: CALL whisper.walk($v) YIELD coverage, host, nearest_known_vendors, no_atlas_match, siblings

tools.name: whisper_explain
tools.description: Score an indicator against the threat feeds and explain exactly why. Threat-intel scorer: score + level + human explanation + the feeds it is listed in (feedId, weight, firstSeen/lastSeen). Two live forms: bare CALL explain($v) (full columns) and CALL whisper.explain($v) (restricted YIELD).

_exec.cypher: CALL whisper.explain($v) YIELD indicator, score, level, explanation, sources
_exec.altForm: CALL explain($v) is the same engine, bare form (no whisper. prefix, no YIELD); it returns the fuller column set: indicator, type, available, cached, found, score, level, explanation, factors, sources, advisory.

tools.name: whisper_submit
tools.description: Contribute an indicator observation or feedback back into the graph (requires an API key). The write channel: submit an indicator/feedback with an attributable API key (anonymous submits are refused to preserve K-anonymity). Keyed-only by design.

_exec.altForm: kind:'feedback' takes {observation_id?, query?, results?, comment?, severity?, v?} - all optional, a comment-only report is accepted - and returns the 4-column receipt: observation_id, accepted, advisory, v. Batch: UNWIND $records AS rec CALL whisper.submit(rec) dispatches one call per record, each row in its kind's shape.
_exec.note: WRITE channel; needs an API key carrying the submit:write scope (anonymous callers get a clear 400: a write channel requires an attributable API key, preserving K-anonymity). Per-kind CLOSED arg schema, live-verified: kind:'indicator' allows {kind, identifier_kind, value, observation_id?, confidence?, first_seen?, provenance?, v?} and requires identifier_kind + value; kind:'feedback' allows {kind, observation_id?, query?, results?, comment?, severity?, v?}. identifier_kind is one of ip, asn, cert_sha256, cert_ja3_hash, cert_ja4_hash, cert_jarm, cidr, whois_pattern (plaintext, normalized server-side) or host_hash_rotating, url_path_hash (submitter-side pre-hashed 64-char SHA-256 hex; a plaintext host/URL is rejected, never auto-hashed). results is a list of strings. An unknown key or kind is rejected with a clear 400 naming the allowed set.
